Fixture: 110_noise_rgb_32x32.jxl
32x32 RGB, VarDCT lossy d=1.0, kNoise set (--photon_noise_iso=3200)

Purpose
-------
K.5 noise synthesis at its smallest expressible size. 32x32 with the default
group_dim (256) is one group, one LF group, one TOC section: a wrong seed
formula, a wrong XorShift128Plus state update, or a wrong group-tile boundary
has nothing else to hide behind. `--photon_noise_iso` is cjxl's flag for
setting frame_header.flags.kNoise and writing a K.5.1 NoiseParameters LUT;
nothing else in the available oracle build exposes that flag.

Frame structure, as parsed by JPXL itself:

  frame 0  kRegularFrame  kVarDCT  frame 32x32 -> output 32x32
           group_dim 256, 1 group, 1 LF group, 1 TOC section
           upsampling 1; flags.kNoise set

Source content is a smooth two-axis gradient (R = x ramp, G = y ramp, B =
128 constant) so the K.5.2 strength LUT -- keyed off the pre-noise X/Y
samples via in_R = (Y+X)/2, in_G = (Y-X)/2 -- sweeps through more than one
LUT bucket across the image, rather than sampling the same strength
everywhere a flat source would give.

Grading (18181-3 4.2)
---------------------
Filters are left at cjxl's own choice (Annex A's ordinary error class):

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.02,  RMSE <= 1e-3   (filters enabled)

The corpus `noise`/`noise_5` case is the primary evidence (500x606,
multi-group, graded at its own tight test.json thresholds, peak <= 0.004 /
RMSE <= 1e-4 -- effectively a bit-exactness contract per K.5.2's own NOTE1).
This handmade fixture is the smallest-case debugging rung, not a replacement
for it: see crates/jpxl-decode/tests/e2e_noise.rs.

  cjxl flags:   -d 1.0 -e 7 --photon_noise_iso=3200 --modular=0
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-noise-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

                sha256 92c73a0c0ee7880a3184789718172c88d477d8166b31ffb4a3242d0297dc1fb5

                sha256 6e9ac25eeca9a4d59478714bc5a7f6340321f3434b739299e769daac02a0d062

  Reference decode (djxl --output_format npy):
    110_noise_rgb_32x32.npy  (12366 bytes)
    sha256 7f66b92b675df1de5e78c871d59a9af688be92c005b260a14235c8367dab9180
    Committed alongside the fixture (< 100 KB).
    Shape (1, 32, 32, 3) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. Readable with
    jpxl_conformance::FloatImage::from_npy.
    Regenerable at any time from the fixture with the pinned djxl build
    (decode is deterministic per libjxl revision, see PINNED_REVISIONS.txt).

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
